proofReview.fixedCenter: Deleting negative leaves improves the score; deleting zero leaves preserves it. Exchanging a selected smaller positive neighbor for an unselected larger neighbor preserves legality and cannot reduce the score. Thus the largest up-to-k positive neighbor values give the best score for a fixed center.
proofReview.global: Every nonempty star has a center considered by the algorithm. Every generated score is attainable by a valid star. Taking the maximum over all centers is therefore exact. Initializing from the largest node value correctly preserves all-negative and k=0 cases.
proofReview.complexityAndIntegers: Reference adjacency sorting costs O(n+m log(m+1)) conservatively, uses O(n+m) space, and the maximum result is at most100000000 while the minimum optimum is at least-1000. Full original domain is supported without reducing k to n-1.
proofReview.artifactBindings: Import schema and normalized checksum verified. Batch editorial exactly equals displayed editorial; authored solutions match displayed solutions, and displayed Python code exactly matches reference bytes. Standalone correctness-proof heading present.

independentVerification.preFreezeDomain: Every nonempty simple graph on2..4 vertices, every assignment from{-1,0,2}, and k=0..n. Enumerated all centers and leaf subsets; all agree with positive-neighbor selection. Independent original examples120/16 and triangle result6 also checked.
independentVerification.smallArtifactMethod: Enumerate every center and every subset of its actual neighbors with subset size<=k. Directly sum weights, retaining empty leaf sets and negative centers. Used on197 actual formal/oracle cases.
independentVerification.largeArtifactMethod: Independent value-domain order-statistic search: for each center binary-search the kth largest positive neighbor threshold in1..1000 by counting qualifying values, then sum values strictly above the threshold and add the necessary threshold copies. No sorted adjacency lists, global vertex bucket ordering, or reference function calls. Used on all11 full-scale graphs.
